What we do

Eight programmes, one occupational health partner

Each one can be bought on its own. Run together, they share a single employee record, a single reporting calendar and a single point of accountability.

Health Surveillance

Pre-employment, pre-placement and periodic medical examinations, biological monitoring and investigation of suspected occupational disease — run as a programme, not a one-off clinic day.

Corporate Health Programmes

Site health risk assessment, ERC-qualified first aid training, site emergency planning, and BLS & ALS equipment and ambulance provision.

Applying ergonomic principles to the workplace to reduce musculoskeletal disorders and the compensation claims that follow — while improving productivity, quality and efficiency.

Mental Health & Employee Support

Promoting positive mental health and reducing the stigma around workplace stress, through workshops, individual sessions and a three-gear method of awareness, response and collaboration.

Why Occuo Health

Occupational health that changes the workplace, not just the filing cabinet

Most providers sell examinations. We sell the reduction in risk that the examinations are supposed to produce — and we report on whether it happened.

On your site, not in our waiting room

Mobile teams and portable diagnostics mean examinations happen where your people already are. No travel time, no lost shifts, far higher attendance.

Built around compliance obligations

Programmes are scoped against Egyptian Labour Law No. 12 of 2003 and its executive regulations, and mapped to ISO 45001 and client HSE requirements where those apply.

Confidentiality that is actually enforced

Clinical detail stays with the physician. Employers receive fitness decisions and anonymised aggregates — a boundary we do not negotiate.

Reported against a baseline

We measure before we intervene and re-measure after. If a programme is not moving its metric, that shows up in the review rather than being quietly absorbed.

One provider, one record

Surveillance, ergonomics, mental health and emergency readiness under one contract, with one employee record — instead of four vendors and four spreadsheets.

Arabic and English throughout

Examinations, workshops, coaching and written material delivered in both languages, adapted for field and shift-based workforces.

How we work

Assess before you buy anything

A five-stage cycle that starts with your hazards and ends with a review against the numbers we set at the beginning.

01

Assess

We walk the site, review your hazard register and incident history, and establish what your exposures actually are — before proposing anything.

02

Design

A written programme scoped to those exposures: protocols, intervals, roles covered, deliverables and a cost you can budget against.

03

Deliver

Examinations, training and interventions run on a fixed calendar, mostly on-site, scheduled around your shift pattern.

04

Report

Fitness decisions to managers, anonymised trends to HSE and HR, and an audit-ready record set to your retention schedule.

05

Review

Scheduled programme review against the baseline metrics, with the scope adjusted as your operation and its risks change.

Sectors

Built around how each sector actually works

A construction site at peak phase, a rotating-shift plant and a corporate head office share almost none of the same risks. The programme should not be the same either.

Manufacturing & FMCG

Production-line ergonomics, noise and chemical surveillance, shift-fatigue management and on-site clinic cover.

Construction & Infrastructure

Work-at-height and confined-space medicals, site first aid capability, standby cover for peak phases.

Oil, Gas & Petrochemicals

Remote-site medical cover, medevac planning, biological monitoring and emergency responder fitness.

Pharmaceutical & Chemical

Exposure-specific biological monitoring, cleanroom health protocols and occupational disease investigation.

Logistics & Transport

Driver medical fitness, sleep apnoea screening, fatigue and journey-management risk programmes.

Corporate & Services

Display-screen ergonomics, mental health and coaching programmes, executive health checks.

In practice

What clients say

The programmes that work are the ones that survive contact with a live operation — a running production line, a turnaround, a night shift.

  • Mobilisation in two to three weeks for a standard scope
  • Examinations scheduled around your shift pattern, not ours
  • Reporting clean enough to hand to a parent-company audit

Questions

The things employers ask us first

Labour Law No. 12 of 2003 and its executive regulations place duties on employers covering occupational health provision, medical examination of workers exposed to hazards, record keeping and the reporting of occupational disease. The specific obligations depend on your sector, headcount and hazard profile — we scope every programme against the obligations that actually apply to you rather than a generic checklist.

Predominantly on-site. Mobile teams with portable audiometry, spirometry and phlebotomy handle the large majority of examinations at your location, which removes travel time and lifts attendance rates substantially. Specialist referrals and diagnostics run through our clinic network.

Clinical findings stay between the examining physician and the employee. The employer receives a fitness-to-work decision — fit, fit with restrictions, or temporarily unfit — together with anonymised aggregate reporting at group sizes that prevent re-identification.

Yes. Multi-site programmes run on a single protocol set and a single employee record system, with a shared reporting calendar so central HSE sees consistent data from every location.

There is no fixed minimum. Smaller employers typically start with a health risk assessment plus pre-employment medicals, then extend the scope once the risk picture is clear. Larger sites usually contract an annual programme.
